result:
REST wins on: HTTP caching (CDNs, browser cache, standard tooling), simplicity (URLs are discoverable, HTTP verbs familiar), debugging (curl/browser). Loses on: N+1 requests (fetch user → posts → comments per post), over-fetching (you get all fields even if you need 3), mobile bandwidth.

GraphQL wins on: single request for exactly the fields you need, no over/under-fetching, mobile efficiency. Loses on: HTTP caching dead (most queries POST with bodies), query complexity can DoS the server (unbounded nesting/aliases), steeper learning curve, harder to debug (queries aren't URLs).

**Verdict:** REST for public, cacheable, mostly-simple data; GraphQL for mobile-first, high-churn schemas, or complex internal consumption. Start with REST unless you have the mobile/schema-churn problem now. If you hit N+1 walls later, add a GraphQL layer on top (BFF).
